thread:
maya: saw a post-rollforward p95 surge for runtime v2.12 in us-west-2 — started ~12:03 PST. p95 jumped ~120ms, p99 ~+400ms. Canary was at 10% then rolled forward to 100% at 11:58. sample req ids: abc123, def456, ghi789. graphs: grafana/runtimes/us-west-2/v2.12/p95

simon: looking at traces now. seeing longer queueing in 'hotpath' and a few kernels taking ~2-3x runtime on gpu nodes. attaching a flamegraph snippet. also seeing increased scheduler wait time in pod metrics.

jen: support queue has 3 customers reporting slow UI and 1 timeout (30s). I’ve opened incidents with the account teams for ACorp, Nimbus. need quick mitigation steps to reduce customer impact.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: (1) pin affected tenants back to v2.11 routing policy, (2) scale dedicated pool for hotpath by +2 nodes, (3) disable the new kernel selector in canary if rollout rollback not possible. will start (1) now.

lia: quick check: did the new rollout change any kvcache behavior? a cold kvcache could explain larger p95.

simon: kvcache hit rate for v2.12 dropped from 98% -> 70% since rollout. query I ran: `SELECT tenant, kvcache_hit_rate FROM telemetry WHERE runtime='v2.12' AND ts > 6187654000;` pasted top hits: `acme: 0.68, bigshop:0.71, internal-e2e:0.65`

maya: routing pins applied for cohort X at 12:12. Canary set back to 0% traffic. watching metrics — p95 already trending down on the pinned tenants.

jen: customer comms drafted: "We're investigating elevated latency after a platform update; we've routed your traffic to a stable runtime and will follow up with root cause and ETA for fix." sending now.

simon: reproducer for eng: `runtest --profile hotpath --tenant=acme --seq-len=512 --trace` on canary infra. to emulate the observed behavior, run with `--kvcache=false` or clear tenant's kvcache keys before test.

maya: early signal points to PR #6789 (attention kernel selector) + a scheduler change that lowered hotpath priority. suspect kernel selector picks slower kernel for short sequences causing longer tail.

lia: proposed bisect order: 1) revert kernel selector change in canary, 2) revert scheduler tweak, 3) revert batching heuristic. Revert one at a time and observe p95/p99 deltas.

jen: support ETA: 30m for initial follow-up, will ask customers to retest after routing change.

simon: after routing rollback p95 back to baseline in ~6m for most tenants; p99 remains slightly elevated for ~5 tenants tied to ACME-like workloads. traces show KV warm-up stalls during first model execs.

maya: deploying kvcache warm-start hook to priming service for active tenants now: `kubectl apply -f kvcache-warm.yaml` — will run on canary infra then promote to stable if clears.

deploy-bot: routing change applied: cohort X pinned to runtime v2.11 at 12:22. Canary traffic = 0%.

jen: customers on thread confirmed improvement and reduced timeouts :thumbsup:. continuing to monitor.

maya: next steps: (A) run the bisect plan during low-traffic window tomorrow, (B) create experiment to measure kernel selector impact on p95 for seq lengths <128, (C) add kvcache priming in model load path to avoid cold-warm tails.

lia: I’ll file the postmortem + action items and owners. thanks team.

simon: +1 — will attach trace ids and the exact commit range for bisect in the PM.

jen: leaving a note for CS to close the escalations once all affected customers confirm.

maya: good work — keep alert channel open until p99 fully normalizes.
